name: Week 30 Legs — Heels Up at 45, Flat at 80, RDL Drops to 45
description:
**The heel plates move down to the warmup, where they can actually teach something.** Elevated at 80 turned into a different exercise rather than a deeper one, so this week the plates go under the 45 ramp — learn the position where depth is free, then bring it to the working weight later. **All three sets at 80 run flat.**

**The barbell RDL drops to 45/side, by your call.** At 70 the set ended when the grip gave out; at 45 it ends when the hinge does, which is the limiter worth training while the movement is still new. **The full form walkthrough is in the notes.**

**Kneeling leg curl holds 65** with one new cue. **Hip abduction goes to 250.** Leg press, calf raise and adduction hold.

dayOverview.theme: Two deliberate steps back that are both steps forward: the heel plates move to a weight where they can teach the position, and the RDL drops to a weight where form is the limiter instead of grip. Everything else holds, and the leg press gets the spotlight for the depth it has quietly been gaining.

spotlights.why: Dropping to 45 was your call and it is the right one — the set now ends on the hinge rather than the hands. Full setup-to-finish walkthrough this week, because a lighter bar is when form is worth installing.
Depth has been improving quietly for weeks — knees to chest on every set now, including the first. Worth checking whether that holds when nothing about it is new.

dayOverview.rotationPlan: W31 — spotlight moves to the kneeling leg curl and the hip machines. W32 — Bulgarian split squat and the Nordic curl return when the week stops being short (both are big DOMS producers, which is exactly why they stay out of compressed weeks).
watchpoints: 🛑 keep it shy — the cue is the cap: squat, barbell RDL, leg press, kneeling leg curl, hip abduction, hip adduction. Effort means the cue holding at a hard load; the ceiling is the rep the cue breaks.
🔥 near-failure last set OK: leg press calf raise. Isolation work where form holds at the limit.
**Never judge the squat on set 1.** Set 2 has been stronger and deeper three weeks running. Set 1 is information, not a verdict.
**The heel plates are at 45 now, not 80.** Learn the deep position where the load is not in the way, then take it up. Heels-up at 80 comes back when the 45 version is boring.
**Stance is settled — do not test it.** The current wide V beats feet-forward and beats going wider. That question is closed.
**RDL is double-overhand at 45.** No flipped hand, no straps. At this weight the hamstrings should end the set — if the grip is still what stops you, say so, because that changes the read.
**Kneeling leg curl: only the lower leg moves.** When the front of the working hip joins in to finish the rep, that rep was the last one.

sets.name: Legs Warmup — Ankle First, Then the Heel-Elevated Ramp
sets.notes: The ankle work leads because the ankle is the confirmed limiter. **The ramp round is where the heel plates live this week** — five paused reps at 45 with the heels up is the whole heel-elevation project for now.

exercises.notes: Slow up, slow down — feel the shin.
Toe to wall, knee bent, heel glued down. **No measurement this week** — the baseline is banked at right 1.5 fists, left 1 fist, and the re-measure is about a month out.
Light band, eversion only — slow and controlled. The left one is the point.
Eyes open, hands on hips. Let the ankle do the correcting.
Your usual stance — the wide V, no experiments. Heels down, chest up, knees out. Note where depth stops today.
Small to large, warm the joint.
**The brace, woken deliberately.** It is half the answer to the depth question — bring it online before the bar.

**LOAD:** 45/side, two rounds.

**Round 1 — flat, 5 reps, 2-3s pause in the bottom.** The standard you already set.

**Round 2 — 5lb plate under each heel, 5 reps, 2-3s pause.** This is the new slot for the heel elevation.
- **Go as deep as the position now allows** — with the heels up there should be more room, and the point is to use it
- **Stay upright and let the knees travel forward** — that is what the elevation buys, and it is why it feels like the front of the thighs
- **Hold the brace through the pause**, ribs down
- Compare it to round 1 honestly: deeper, or just different?

sets.name: Squat — 80/side, All Three Flat 🛑
sets.notes:
**LOAD:** 80/side, 3 working sets of 6-8. **All flat — the plates stay in the warmup this week.**

- **Set 1 is information, not a verdict.** It has read shallow three weeks running and set 2 has been better every time
- **Belt-tight brace** — ribs down, glutes and core braced, shoulders packed down
- **Depth is the descent** — find where power falls off in the hole and work into it, not past it
- **The pelvis tucking under is the floor.** Stop just above where it starts; that edge is what moves over months
- 80 has read "like what 45s were before" two weeks running. That is the floor rising, and it needs nothing done to it

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 80/side, 3 sets, all flat.
- Usual wide V stance, no experiments
- Belt-tight brace, ribs down, shoulders packed down
- Depth is the job, not the load
- Stop just above where the pelvis starts to tuck

sets.name: 🔆 Barbell RDL — 45/side, Form Reset 🛑
sets.notes:
**LOAD:** 45/side on the bar, 3 sets of 8-10. **Straight after the squat — the bar is already there.**

**🔆 SPOTLIGHT — the full walkthrough you asked for. Lighter bar, so the attention goes on the movement.**

**Setup:**
- **Start standing.** Take the bar out of the hooks at about mid-thigh — do not deadlift it off the floor to begin
- **Double-overhand, both palms facing you, thumbs wrapped around the bar.** No mixed grip, no straps
- **The bar sits low in the hand, in the finger crease**, not up in the palm — high in the palm is what rolls open when the grip tires
- **Squeeze the bar hard before you unrack it** and keep squeezing

**The movement:**
- **Set a soft knee bend once, at the start, and do not change it.** Bending more as you descend turns it into a squat
- **Push the hips BACK, like closing a car door with your backside.** The bar goes down because the hips went back, not because you bent forward
- **The bar brushes the thighs the whole way down** — if it drifts away from your legs, your back is taking the load
- **Shoulders packed DOWN**, lats squeezing the bar into the legs, chest proud, neutral neck
- **Stop where the hamstrings stop you** — the moment you feel the stretch run out, that is the bottom. Going lower only comes from rounding the back
- **Stand up by driving the hips forward**, and **stop at straight.** No leaning back at the top

**Tempo:** 3 seconds down, no pause needed, smooth up.

**Common faults:** squatting it down · the bar drifting off the thighs · rounding at the bottom to chase depth · hyperextending at the top.

**Reflection:** at 45, what ends the set — the hamstrings, or still the grip?

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 45/side on the bar.
- **Unrack standing from mid-thigh hooks**
- **Double-overhand, bar low in the fingers, squeeze before you lift**
- **Soft knees set once**, hips back like closing a car door
- **Bar brushes the thighs**, lats holding it in
- **3s eccentric**, stop where the hamstrings stop
- Stand to straight and stop — no lean back

sets.name: Kneeling Leg Curl — 65, Only the Lower Leg Moves 🛑
sets.notes:
**LOAD:** 65, 3 sets of 10-12 each side. **Left side first, and the left sets the rep count.**

**The new cue: only the lower leg moves.** The side sensation low near the hip is the hip flexor joining in to finish the curl when the hamstring runs out — so the hips hiking or twisting is the rep ending, not a brace exercise.

- Same load both sides; match the right to the left's clean reps
- **Hips stay flat and square** — the moment the working hip lifts or rotates, that rep was the last one
- Slow eccentric — that is the stimulus
- **Log both sides separately**

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 65.
- **Left side first**
- **Only the lower leg moves** — hips flat and square
- Slow eccentric
- When the front of the hip joins in, the set is done
- Log both sides separately

sets.name: 🔆 Leg Press — 4 Plates/Side, Knees to Chest 🛑
sets.notes:
**LOAD:** 4 plates/side, 4 sets of 12.

**🔆 SPOTLIGHT — the quiet one.** Depth has improved here for weeks without anything being done to it: knees to chest on every set now, first set included, and the last set keeps opening up further. Nothing changes this week — the question is whether that holds when it is not new.

- **Deep ROM — work depth, not weight**
- **Ribs down, no leaning back**
- **The end-range stretch deep in the hips is the position, not a problem** — the spine is unloaded here, which is why this is a safe place to live at end range
- **Do not read this depth as permission at 80 on the bar** — they are different problems
- Set 1 has stopped being the bad set. Notice whether that is still true

**Reflection:** did the first set arrive deep again, and did the last set still open up further than the rest?

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 4 plates/side, 4 sets.
- **Deep ROM** — depth, not weight
- Ribs down, no leaning back
- Knees to chest is the standard
- Slow into the bottom, no bouncing out of it

sets.name: Leg Press Calf Raise — 4 Plates/Side 🔥
sets.notes:
**LOAD:** 4 plates/side, 3 sets of 15. **Same machine — stay where you are.**

- Balls of the feet on the bottom platform edge, heels off
- **Full controlled heel drop** — the slow stretch is the stimulus
- Press through the forefoot to a full contraction
- Knees stay soft and still
- Last set can run near failure

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 4 plates/side.
- Full controlled heel drop
- Press through the forefoot
- Knees soft and still

sets.name: Hip Abduction Machine — 250 🛑
sets.notes:
**LOAD:** 250, 2 sets of 12-15. You found this one yourself last week and it read easy.

- **Tempo is the only lever** — slow out, slow back, no bouncing off the stack
- **If set 1 at 250 is still easy at that tempo, take the next pin on set 2** and log which one
- Torso quiet — no rocking to start the rep

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 250.
- **Tempo is the only lever**
- Slow out, slow back, torso quiet
- Next pin on set 2 if the tempo holds — log which

sets.name: Hip Adduction Machine — 300 🛑
sets.notes:
**LOAD:** 300, 2 sets of 12-15.

- **Tempo is the only lever**
- Slow release out to a full stretch — the adductors are the tissue that capped the wide-stance test, so the stretch end matters here
- Torso still, no rocking

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 300.
- **Tempo is the only lever**
- Slow release to a full stretch
- Torso still

sets.name: Cool-Down — 5 Min Fascia/Recovery Block
sets.notes: Five minutes, every gym day. Slow breathing throughout — the downshift is as much the point as the tissue.

exercises.notes: 30s each arm, elbow at MID height.
Passive. Let the shoulders decompress.
30s each side.
45s each side.
Slow breathing. End here.

tips: Heel plates are in the warmup at 45 this week, not under the working sets.
RDL is 45/side. Read the walkthrough before the first set — that is what the lighter bar is for.
Leg curl: only the lower leg moves. Hips flat and square.
Abduction starts at 250; take the next pin on set 2 if the slow tempo holds.
Log the leg curl's two sides separately.
